lines.text: Anthropic just lost $80.7 billion. In six months.
lines.say: Anthropic just lost eighty point seven billion dollars. In six months!

lines.text: And yet, investors want to value it at up to $2 trillion.
lines.say: And yet, investors want to value it at up to two trillion dollars.

lines.text: One of these numbers is mostly an illusion. And the number that could really sink it isn’t on screen yet.
lines.say: One of these numbers is mostly an illusion. And the number that could really sink it... isn't on screen yet.

lines.text: First: how strong is Anthropic, really?
At the start of 2025, its revenue was running at about $1 billion a year. By July 2026: $65 billion.
lines.say: At the start of twenty twenty-five, its revenue was running at about one billion dollars a year. By July twenty twenty-six: sixty-five billion.

lines.text: Its CEO said they planned for 10x growth, and got 80x.
lines.say: Its CEO said they planned for ten-x growth, and got eighty-x.

lines.text: That’s ahead of OpenAI, reportedly at around $40 billion.
lines.say: That's ahead of OpenAI, reportedly at around forty billion.

lines.text: One survey, by Menlo Ventures, an Anthropic investor, gave it 40% of enterprise AI-model spending, and 54% of coding.
lines.say: One survey, by Menlo Ventures, an Anthropic investor, gave it forty percent of enterprise AI model spending, and fifty-four percent of coding.

lines.text: Amazon put in about $13 billion. That stake is now marked at roughly $190 billion.
lines.say: Amazon put in about thirteen billion dollars. That stake is now marked at roughly one hundred and ninety billion.

lines.text: Its valuation? $61.5 billion in March 2025.
lines.say: Its valuation? Sixty-one and a half billion, in March twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: $965 billion this May. Now, IPO talk of up to $2 trillion.
lines.say: Nine hundred and sixty-five billion, this May. Now, IPO talk of up to two trillion.

lines.text: Then the draft IPO filing leaked, with three numbers that stunned Wall Street.
Revenue, first half of 2026: $16.3 billion.
lines.say: Revenue, for the first half of twenty twenty-six: sixteen point three billion.

lines.text: Net loss: $80.7 billion.
lines.say: Net loss: eighty point seven billion.

lines.text: Cash and short-term investments, end of 2025: $20.28 billion.
lines.say: Cash and short-term investments, end of twenty twenty-five: twenty point two eight billion.

lines.text: That loss is $13.5 billion a month. At that rate, twenty billion lasts about 45 days.
lines.say: That loss is thirteen and a half billion dollars a month. At that rate, twenty billion lasts about forty-five days.

lines.text: Dead by Valentine’s Day. So… why isn’t it?
lines.say: Dead by Valentine's Day. So... why isn't it?

lines.text: Because about $72 billion of that loss never left the building.
lines.say: Because about seventy-two billion of that loss never left the building.

lines.text: It’s an accounting charge on convertible notes: money investors lent that turns into shares later.
lines.say: It's an accounting charge on convertible notes. Money investors lent, that turns into shares later.

lines.text: Picture it: a friend lends you $10, and you promise to repay in your company’s shares, at today’s price.
lines.say: Picture it. A friend lends you ten dollars, and you promise to repay in your company's shares, at today's price.

lines.text: Your company becomes ten times more valuable. Those shares are now worth $100.
lines.say: Your company becomes ten times more valuable. Those shares are now worth a hundred dollars.

lines.text: On paper, you just lost $90. In cash, you spent nothing.
lines.say: On paper, you just lost ninety dollars. In cash, you spent nothing.

lines.text: Anthropic’s valuation jumped about two and a half times in three months. The notes got pricier, and the reported loss exploded.
lines.say: Anthropic's valuation jumped about two and a half times, in three months. So the notes got pricier, and the reported loss exploded.

lines.text: The stronger Anthropic gets, the more money it appears to lose.
The proof: that same quarter, Amazon marked those very notes up by $55.7 billion.
lines.say: The proof? That same quarter, Amazon marked those very notes up by fifty-five point seven billion dollars.

lines.text: Strip the charge out, and the $80 billion loss shrinks to under $9 billion.
lines.say: Strip the charge out, and the eighty billion dollar loss shrinks to under nine.

lines.text: So the loss is fake?
Not so fast. There’s a number in the filing that is very, very real.
lines.say: Not so fast. There's a number in the filing that is very, very real.

lines.text: Compute. Its half-year compute bill went from $2.3 billion to nearly $9 billion.
lines.say: Compute. Its half-year compute bill went from two point three billion dollars, to nearly nine billion.

lines.text: And the filing reportedly lists at least $518 billion in AI-infrastructure commitments over roughly a decade.
lines.say: And the filing reportedly lists at least five hundred and eighteen billion dollars in AI infrastructure commitments, over roughly a decade.

lines.text: Google. Amazon. Microsoft. Nvidia chips. Broadcom-linked leases.
lines.say: Google. Amazon. Microsoft. Nvidia chips. Broadcom-linked leases.

lines.text: About 80% of it can’t be cancelled.
lines.say: About eighty percent of it, can't be cancelled.

lines.text: Now put the cash next to it. The bill is about 25 times bigger.
lines.say: Now put the cash next to it. The bill is about twenty-five times bigger.

lines.text: Yes, that cash figure is from December, and $95 billion in new funding has been announced since. Still a fraction of the bill.
lines.say: Yes, that cash figure is from December, and ninety-five billion dollars in new funding has been announced since. Still, a fraction of the bill.

lines.text: Its compute landlords are also its investors, and, the filing warns, increasingly its rivals.
lines.say: Its compute landlords are also its investors... and, the filing warns, increasingly its rivals.

lines.text: And roughly a fifth to a quarter of revenue comes from just two customers.
So: strong, or fragile? Valuations range from $144 billion to $2 trillion.
lines.say: So. Strong, or fragile? Valuations range from one hundred and forty-four billion, to two trillion.

lines.text: Look at those three numbers again.
$16.3 billion in revenue: real demand.
lines.say: Sixteen point three billion in revenue. Real demand.

lines.text: $80.7 billion in losses: mostly the price of success.
lines.say: Eighty point seven billion in losses. Mostly, the price of success.

lines.text: $20.28 billion in cash: a snapshot, not a runway.
lines.say: Twenty point two eight billion in cash. A snapshot, not a runway.

lines.text: That’s why it’s going public. It needs the deepest pool of capital on Earth.
lines.say: That's why it's going public. It needs the deepest pool of capital on Earth.

lines.text: Anthropic’s strength is real. So is the bill. The only question is which one grows faster.
lines.say: Anthropic's strength is real. So is the bill. The only question is... which one grows faster.
